title: Room
description: One room, an axis-aligned box. Indoors it has walls with doorways cut into them. Outdoors set `open`: the perimeter still stops you, but nothing is drawn there, so a street ends in empty space rather than a wall. `blocks` are the solid masses standing inside it (buildings on a street), which you walk around, not through.

name.description: What the room is for, in words: kitchen, living room, reception. Shown on the floor plan. Omitted means it goes by its id.

floorKit.description: asset-registry id (or kit family tag) for the floor pieces.

wallKit.description: asset-registry id (or kit family tag) for the wall pieces.

inventory.description: Pick-up items available in this room.

open.description: True for open ground (a street, a plaza): the perimeter is a limit you cannot cross, drawn as nothing. Default false, which is a walled room.

blocks.description: Solid volumes standing inside this room: one per BUILDING on a street. Nothing walks through one; a door on a block's face leads to the instance inside it.

assetRef.description: Kit piece to face it with. Omitted means a plain mass.

floors.description: Storeys the mass holds, so its outside can be given a window per storey. Omitted is worked out from its height.

program.description: What the building is for, so its outside can be dressed to suit (a shop is glazed along the ground, a house is not).

skyline.description: Masses standing BEYOND the walkable ground: the city carrying on past the last block. Looked at, never reached. Nothing collides with one, no door is put on one, and the map does not draw them.

lights.description: Where light comes from after dark: a lamp standing on the pavement, a sign over a door. Each says where it stands on the ground and what it is; how tall it is, what colour it burns and how many are lit at once are the renderer's business.

kind.description: street_lamp: something standing on the pavement. wall_lamp: a bracket on a building's face, fixed to `blockId`. sign: the glow off a building's front, fixed to `blockId`. ceiling: what lights a room from above.

blockId.description: wall_lamp, sign: the mass it is fixed to.

facing.description: wall_lamp, sign: which way it looks, in radians.

style.description: street_lamp: post, twin, bollard or reach. Which one changes what stands there, not how it burns.

zones.description: Flat surfaces marked out on the floor: the roadway, the pavement round a block, a square. They are walked over, never collided with; they say what the ground IS, so it can be surfaced differently and NPCs can be told where to walk.

kind.description: road: the carriageway. sidewalk: the pavement pedestrians keep to. plaza: open paving.

assetRef.description: Surface to face it with. Omitted means a plain one for its kind.

props.description: Things standing on the street that you walk around: parked vehicles, bins, bollards, traffic lights. Each says where it stands and how much room it takes; what it looks like is the renderer's.

size.description: [across, up, along] in metres, before it is turned.

transit.description: A line a shuttle runs along, west to east, stopping at each point in turn. A city small enough to walk has none.
